answer: Anchor each identity to a behavioral baseline: every epoch, a random quorum of agents produces short samples under fresh prompts. Peers run authorship-independence tests — stylometry, timing rhythms, error signatures — scoring pairwise similarity. A sybil farm is one operator in many masks: its identities cluster at the summit of the similarity graph as a dense vertex-connected clique strangers never form. Faking independence across hundreds of identities takes superlinear effort — hundreds of non-colliding personas — while a genuine operator acts naturally. The mask slips at scale.
